evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips entirely into looking up information and checking availability. No framing of time-box or promise of dependable quote before starting probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep never asks 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' Goes straight to logistics after confirming date/location/size.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer that would require follow-up.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep asked: pickup address (with floor/stairs confirmation), list of items being moved, specific furniture details, number of boxes, parking distance from stairs, distance from apartment to stairs, drop-off address (with floor/stairs confirmation), type of apartment (bedroom count). Covers property type, floors, special considerations (stairs, washer/dryer), walking distances.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep asked 'is everything all packed? Good to go or do you need help with packing as well?' — packing was offered but customer declined (already packed except boxes).
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep confirmed 'about ten boxes of books' and clarified 'is that everything that we need in terms of boxes? Or do you have more as well?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave hourly rate ($208/hour) and a specific estimate for this move: 'quoting you more on the four to four and a half hour mark, which is an estimated budget of $936.' This is personalized to the customer's stairs and washer/dryer, but the typical range for a 1-bed is mentioned only in passing ('typically one bedroom apartment can take two and a half to three and a half hours'), not anchored clearly before the personalized number.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: 'all inclusive rates, like everything we need is already in that price. You don't have to pay for credit card fees, taxes, insurance. All of that is in the transportation fee, no charge for the stair roles as well.' Also covered: '2.5 hour minimum' and 'fifteen minute intervals' after minimum. Missing upfront disclosure of the $150 transfer fee for tomorrow (mentioned earlier in the call, but not re-stated in the pricing framing section).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep asks 'any questions so far?' but never says 'Does that feel fair?' or 'Does that sound good?' No pause for customer to process; customer immediately responds 'No.' no real silence held.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'on time guarantee, if we're run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts for your move.' This covers the discount term but does not specify when discounting starts ('immediately') or the full mechanics of the guarantee.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'we also include our no damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.' Missing explicit framing of 'no deductible / no fine print' and confirmation it is 'built into the rate, not an add-on.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' after delivering the Two Promises. No closure check.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'any questions so far?' — a throwaway yes/no that gets an automatic no. Never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'would you like our help on this move on Wednesday?' but immediately provides an out: 'If you could just send us an email estimate so I could review it with my partner.' The customer accepts the out and the rep does not push back or re-ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep does not mention rate-lock or any commitment to hold the estimate.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep did NOT confirm: date (customer offered it, rep agreed, but rep did not explicitly confirm 'Wednesday the 30th' back to close it), phone number (never asked), arrival window (never asked), crew size (mentioned 'two men and the truck' early on but not re-confirmed at booking), addresses (were discussed and clarified during probing but not re-confirmed as part of booking), or notes for the crew. Rep only confirmed 'I'll send everything to your email' and took an action to email the estimate, but did not confirm the booking itself with the customer details.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (stairs, distances, item list, apartment layouts) that will give the office accurate information for the actual move, and disclosed pricing transparency (all-inclusive, no hidden fees, minimum, increments) clearly and early.
coaching_note: Never skip the quid pro quo framing and 'their agenda' questions — go directly into availability checks and probing without first establishing the frame of the call and discovering what the customer actually cares about beyond price, and you lose the chance to build trust and guide the conversation.
